query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The deposition of a 10 nm thick L1₀ FePt layer on a FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy, followed by annealing at 700°C for 1 hour in vacuum, will increase the coercive field to at least 600 Oe by introducing a hard magnetic layer with high magnetic anisotropy, which will increase the magnetic anisotropy of the high-entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Deposition of 10 nm thick L1₀ FePt layer
generation.conditions: Sputtering at room temperature, followed by annealing at 700°C for 1 hour in vacuum
generation.structural_mediator: Introduction of a hard magnetic layer with high magnetic anisotropy
generation.mechanism: The hard magnetic layer increases the magnetic anisotropy of the high-entropy alloy, leading to increased coercivity
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercive field increased to at least 600 Oe
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative
generation.boundary: The high-entropy alloy must remain in a single-phase fcc structure, and the FePt layer must be compatible with the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The effect of the FePt layer on the overall microstructure and magnetic properties of the high-entropy alloy is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the coercive field of the FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy with and without the FePt layer, using a vibrating sample magnetometer or a superconducting quantum interference device
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the alloy with the FePt layer is not significantly higher than that of the alloy without the FePt layer, the hypothesis is falsified
